headline: Failed House rule that would have set debate terms for four measures, including a bill to change the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act.
what_it_does: This was a procedural rule, which sets how the House debates and votes on other measures. If adopted, it would have allowed House floor votes on four items: H.R. 7888, a bill to change the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978; H.R. 529, a bill to extend U.S. customs waters from 12 to 24 nautical miles offshore; H.Res. 1112, a resolution criticizing the current administration's immigration policies; and H.Res. 1117, a resolution about outside pressure on Israel over Gaza. The rule itself would not have changed any law. Each of those measures would still have needed its own vote.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the House of Representatives
who_it_affects.how: They would have debated and voted on the four listed measures under the terms this rule set.
